If you wanted to know all the jobs that AI will produce, look no further than cybersecurity. This is going to become one of the biggest investment areas for enterprises going forward. 

And even as the work becomes more agentic and autonomous you will need more talent to point the agents at the most critical work, review findings, patch systems, respond to incidents, and more.

We’re entering a new cyber regime, and we’ll probably use 100X more tokens on this loop than we’re imagining right now, because we can scan every log, look at every line of code, look through traffic, and process data at a scale that wasn’t comprehensible before.

More than ever, enterprises are going to care deeply about how they manage their networks, systems, software, data, identity, devices, and more. Agents will largely become the solution to these challenges, but they will keep everyone up in the process.

Ask Hermes to make a 70m poly treasure chest for Godot, or to turn a photo of a mug into a model you can print, and it does the job through Meshy's MCP server.

tweets.text:
Across math, coding, tool use, and terminal tasks, JOLT+ beat GRPO on all five benchmarks, including 9.9 points on AppWorld.

https://t.co/KFHdZ0tuFn https://t.co/rKojjZn1sd

Self-distillation trains only the student. Its teacher can use the extra information to exploit shortcuts unavailable to the student.

JOLT also trains the teacher on outcome rewards from its own attempts, with a penalty when its predictions diverge from the student's.

Reinforcement learning methods like GRPO give one reward per attempt, which doesn't show which steps helped.

Self-distillation adds per-token feedback from a teacher. The same model plays the teacher, with extra information like a verified solution, and the student, without it. https://t.co/PFHljkzvQ5
